benchmark_name: MultiBLiMP 1.0: A Massively Multilingual Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs (MultiBLiMP 1.0)
humanities_role_explanation: Items are grammatical/ungrammatical sentences drawn from Universal Dependencies treebanks in 101 languages (including historical and ancient ones such as Latin, Sanskrit, Ancient Greek); the competence tested is general formal linguistic (morphosyntactic agreement) competence of LMs, not humanities disciplinary competence.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only sentence minimal pairs; the model's probability for the grammatical vs. ungrammatical sentence is compared.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Grammaticality judgment via minimal pairs: the model is scored on whether it assigns higher probability to the grammatical sentence over the minimally different ungrammatical one (subject-verb and subject-participle agreement for number, person, gender). Closest controlled labels are classification/fact_verification (judging well-formedness); no generation or MCQ prompting.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one phenomenon family (subject-verb/subject-participle agreement), though across 101 languages.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 42 LLMs: Llama3 (1B-70B), Tülu3, Aya-expanse, Gemma3, Qwen3, OLMo2, EuroLLM base and chat versions, plus Goldfish monolingual models.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy (higher probability for grammatical sentence) and mean log-probability difference; McNemar tests.

summary: MultiBLiMP 1.0 is an automatically generated benchmark of 128,321 linguistic minimal pairs for subject-verb and subject-participle agreement in 101 languages, built from Universal Dependencies and UniMorph. The authors evaluate 42 LLMs plus monolingual Goldfish models, finding performance driven by model size and language frequency, and degraded by post-training.
key_findings: Llama3-70B-base and Gemma3-27B-base score best at 90.2% average accuracy; performance rises with language frequency; post-training has a negative effect (β = -3.29) while size is positive (β = 4.30); small monolingual Goldfish models significantly beat LLMs on 14 of 101 languages; low-resource and non-Indo-European languages fare worse.
gold_upstream: Universal Dependencies v2.15 (Zeman et al., 2024; Nivre et al., 2016, 2020; de Marneffe et al., 2021) and UniMorph 4.0 (Batsuren et al., 2022); the paper describes them only as resources 'created by a large number of annotators over many years'.
facets_explanation: Minimal pairs are produced by a fully automated pipeline: grammatical sentences come from UD treebanks, and ungrammatical counterparts are made by re-inflecting the verb using UniMorph/UD-derived lexicons. A data-driven collocation test and spot checks validate agreement; the score compares the probability of the grammatical sentence against the one key. The paper does not discuss annotator disagreement.
results_explanation: "Llama3-70B-base and Gemma3-27B-base perform best overall, both scoring 90.2% on average" (accuracy over all 101 languages; Goldfish excluded from the ranking as it covers only 70 languages). The paper states "performance increases with language frequency" and low-resource languages score lower (e.g. Gemma3-27B base 78.3 on low-resource vs 98.0 on high-resource). No human baseline or format comparison is reported.

humanities_role.quote: Our minimal pairs are created using a fully automated pipeline, leveraging the large-scale linguistic resources of Universal Dependencies and UniMorph.

dataset_size.quote: Our procedure results in 128,321 mini-mal pairs across 101 languages.

evaluation_set_size.quote: Our procedure results in 128,321 mini-mal pairs across 101 languages.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: we measure the grammaticality of the predictions of a model based on the probability it assigns to a grammatical sentence versus an ungrammatical one.

gold_source.quote: The creation of MultiBLiMP 1.0 was only possible due to the exis-tence of UD and UniMorph, both large resources created by a large number of annotators over many years.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: a formally competent LM is expected to assign higher probability to the grammatical ver-sion.

answer_multiplicity.quote: The accuracy score is based on the number of items for which the model assigns a higher probability to the grammatical sentence

reported_best_score.quote: Llama3-70B-base and Gemma3-27B-base per-form best overall, both scoring 90.2% on average.

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: For all models, performance increases with language frequency, demonstrating much of the variance in linguistic ability can be explained by data disparity.
